chapter: Bird's world, singers and the new music
title: Billie Holiday as neighbour and friend
summary: She made breakfast for his kids and toured with him through the Midwest.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: Yeah, I got to know her pretty well, because... Well, we lived on 45th Street together, 44th Street rather, in this hotel, and she had an apartment and I had an apartment in the hotel. So she used to come down every morning and fix breakfast for me.
That wasn't the Whitby Apartments, was it?

No, this was on 44th Street. She used to come down when she was in town... She'd wake up early. Like, regardless of what time she went to bed, she'd be up by 9 or 10 o'clock. And she used to come around our house and fix breakfast for the kids and myself -- I had a girl and a boy then. We were all hanging out together. So she used to come by and take the kids out for breakfast or something, or fix breakfast for them and then take them out shopping with her. I couldn't afford to take them shopping every day, but she'd go by and take them shopping as many times as she wanted!

So I told her, 'Look, Billie, I don't appreciate you taking the kids out and buying them a whole lot of things when I can't buy them, because some of the days when they want to go out and get something and you're not here, what am I going to do? I don't have no money to spend like that.' So she told me, she said, 'Well, little Brother, don't pay it no mind. I'm gonna spend my money like I want to.' Ha-ha! So I cracked up behind it. I said, 'Well, that's right. I can't tell you how to spend your money. It's your money.'
But she used to come out and get the kids all the time,
and fix breakfast for me and my old lady and everything. The Lady was somethin' else.

At one time I had a manager named Jud Bernard, and he liked Lady; you know, he thought the world of her. So he booked me on a big with her... Since he was working for me, he got me a gig in St. Louis with Billie. We played a dance there, and then we played one in Chicago and played one in Milwaukee, and one in Gary, Indiana. That's how I really got tight with Lady, and I realized how much talent she really had. Because she really did draw the people in, and the people just loved her -- and I loved her too. And after that, I saw how they really felt about her, and I had thought it was just me feeling that way. But to see other people think that much of her, I'd say, "Gee, she must be doing something right."

But man, she was something else. Boy... After I got off to lead this date, because I had a sextet and she had a rhythm section, you know... So I'd do my bit, and then I'd get off and then she'd come on. And man, I used to stand right there in the wing and just listen to her sing, and say, "God be damned, boy, if I could sing like that I'd be somebody." But it wasn't no use me trying to sing like that. I didn't have no voice compared to what she had, you know. I tried to sing, but it didn't do too good. I even
sang with Andy's band and it still didn't come off too good, but I had a lot of instruments to cover it up, so that nobody knew what was really going on -- besides Andy, of course.
